positions.name: RecordedSettlement
positions.frame: how are settled calibration decisions recorded as ratified items for others to act on?
positions.why: These three expressions cohere under a conviction read of performed settlement: the 'Key decisions:' header (src-3) ratifies what follows as decided, and the two parallel label-value bullets (src-4, src-5) record the instrument and calibration specification as settled items with a verification basis. The formatting itself performs the act of recording decisions, not merely asserting facts — the catalogue structure enacts ratification.

positions.name: CalibrationClaim
positions.frame: how is a completed instrument calibration asserted and its verification grounded?
positions.why: Both expressions are unhedged technical claims by Quill Ashgrove in the same calm-positive, expert register: src-1 asserts the calibration state at a precise frequency, and src-2 grounds that assertion by citing the June reference plates and confirming stability across the full observing band. They share a claim conviction (not performed settlement) and a competence-and-conservation value appeal, cohering as the substantive evidential basis that the decisions catalogue then ratifies.
